In 1943, a dead man fooled Hitler.
The Allies wanted to invade Sicily, but it was the obvious target, and the Germans knew it.
So British spies got a body, and turned him into an officer who never existed. Major William Martin.
They gave him a fake life. Love letters from a fiancee, theater tickets, even a letter from his bank about money he owed.
And chained to him, a briefcase of secret letters, saying the invasion would hit Greece.
A submarine slipped him into the sea off Spain.
He washed ashore, and the letters were copied for German spies, and sent all the way to Hitler.
Hitler believed it. He sent troops and tanks to Greece.
When the Allies landed in Sicily that summer, many of those troops were in the wrong place.
A message reached Churchill. Mincemeat swallowed, rod, line and sinker.
The dead man was a homeless Welshman named Glyndwr Michael. In 1998, his real name was finally added to his grave.
